{{short description|Theorem in probabilistic number theory on additive complex-valued arithmetic functions}}
The '''Turán–Kubilius inequality''' is a [[mathematical theorem]] in [[probabilistic number theory]]. It is useful for proving results about the [[normal order of an arithmetic function]].<ref name="Tenenbaum" />{{Rp|305–308}} The theorem was proved in a [[special case]] in 1934 by [[Pál Turán]] and generalized in 1956 and 1964 by [[Jonas Kubilius]].<ref name="Tenenbaum">{{cite book |last=Tenenbaum |first=Gérald |year=1995 |title=Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory |publisher=Cambridge University Press |volume=46 |series=Cambridge studies in advanced mathematics |isbn=0-521-41261-7}}</ref>{{Rp|316}}

==Statement of the theorem==
This formulation is from [[Gérald Tenenbaum|Tenenbaum]].<ref name="Tenenbaum" />{{Rp|p=302}} Other formulations are in Narkiewicz<ref>{{cite book | last = Narkiewicz | first = Władysław | year = 1983 | title = Number Theory | publisher = World Scientific | location = Singapore | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=4CUUmYrem2YC | isbn = 978-9971-950-13-2}}</ref>{{Rp|p=243}}
and in Cojocaru & Murty.<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Cojocaru | first1 = Alina Carmen | author1-link = Alina Carmen Cojocaru | last2 = Murty | first2 = M. Ram | author2-link = M. Ram Murty | year = 2005 | title = An Introduction to Sieve Methods and Their Applications | publisher = Cambridge University Press | volume = 66 | series = London Mathematical Society Student Texts | isbn = 0-521-61275-6}}</ref>{{Rp|pp=45–46}}

Suppose ''f'' is an [[Additive function|additive]] complex-valued [[arithmetic function]], and write ''p'' for an arbitrary prime and {{math|''&nu;''}} for an arbitrary positive integer. Write

:<math>A(x)=\sum_{p^\nu \le x} f(p^\nu) p^{-\nu}(1-p^{-1})</math>

and

:<math>B(x)^2 = \sum_{p^\nu \le x} \left| f(p^\nu) \right| ^2 p^{-\nu}.</math>

Then there is a function ε(''x'') that goes to zero when ''x'' goes to infinity, and such that for ''x'' ≥ 2 we have

:<math>\frac{1}{x} \sum_{n \le x} |f(n) - A(x)|^2 \le (2 + \varepsilon(x)) B(x)^2. </math>

==Applications of the theorem==
[[Pál Turán|Turán]] developed the inequality to create a simpler proof of the [[Hardy–Ramanujan theorem]] about the [[normal order of an arithmetic function|normal order]] of the number ω(''n'') of distinct prime divisors of an integer ''n''.<ref name="Tenenbaum" />{{Rp|p=316}} There is an exposition of Turán's proof in Hardy & Wright, §22.11.<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Hardy | first1 = G. H. | author1-link = G. H. Hardy | last2 = Wright | first2 = E. M. | author2-link = E. M. Wright | year = 2008 | title = [[An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers]] | edition = Sixth | orig-year = First edition 1938 | others = Revised by [[Roger Heath-Brown|D. R. Heath-Brown]] and [[Joseph H. Silverman]] | publisher = Oxford University Press | location = Oxford, Oxfordshire | isbn = 978-0-19-921986-5}}</ref>
Tenenbaum<ref name="Tenenbaum" />{{Rp|pp=305–308}} gives a proof of the Hardy–Ramanujan theorem using the Turán–Kubilius inequality and states without proof several other applications.
